Sofia Ek Hosts An Immersive Digital Installation of New Audiovisual Book, ‘The Minefield Girl’

by Rachel Lipkin February 2, 2018
by Rachel Lipkin February 2, 2018 0 comments
Sofia Ek’s The Minefield Girl takes on a stimulatory literary hybrid in her new audiovisual book that is something more of a psychedelic and emotional experience.
The Minefield Girl is a memoir and compilation of Ek’s experiences working as a businesswoman in Libya at the height of Muammar Gaddafi’s regime. Ek brought her book more to life by collaborating with 18 artists through the digital art platform, Blackdove. Through the collaboration, a series of moving image art pieces mirror Ek’s story and set a visual context for the listener.
Additionally, Ek collaborated with Buttons NY and Visisonics to create a 3-D sound design to help further express her deeply emotional experience in Libya.
Ek recently hosted an audiovisual experience at The Lightbox in New York City to celebrate the launch of The Minefield Girl ‘s audiovisual version this past Wednesday.

As a financial reporter, journalist Sofia Ek traveled the world, covering economies from Greece to Costa Rica. But not all of her assignments were so scenic; when she was still in her 20s, the Wall Street Journal ’s SmartMoney magazine sent her to report on Libya under Muammar Gaddafi’s tyrannical regime.
